category.targetAudience: High school, science, and engineering students

visualProofs.title: Sum of Cubes: a^3 + b^3 = (a + b)(a^2 - ab + b^2)
visualProofs.shortDescription: Use layered cuboids or signed algebra tiles to balance the added and removed regions.
visualProofs.longDescription: A signed volume model starts with an a+b factor and uses compensating ab layers so the remaining expression multiplies to a^3+b^3.
learningOutcomes: Connect algebraic signs to compensating regions

category.title: Algebraic Identities
category.description: Interactive visual proofs for algebraic identities using square areas, rectangles, factor tiles, expansions, and rearrangements.
category.targetAudience: Middle school, high school, foundation mathematics, engineering entrance preparation

visualProofs.title: Exterior Angle Sum of a Polygon: 360 degrees
visualProofs.shortDescription: Walk around a polygon and accumulate each turning angle.
visualProofs.longDescription: As a walker turns once around any polygon, the total direction change is exactly one full turn, so the exterior angles sum to 360 degrees.

category.title: Geometry Proofs
category.description: Interactive proofs for shapes, angles, circles, polygons, similarity, and area formulas that can be seen and manipulated.
category.targetAudience: School to Engineering Foundation

visualProofs.title: Heron's Formula
visualProofs.shortDescription: Rearrange triangle components and track semiperimeter stages.
visualProofs.longDescription: A visual derivation relates side lengths, altitude, and semiperimeter pieces until the area becomes sqrt(s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)).
learningOutcomes: Explain the structure of Heron's formula

category.title: Geometry Proofs
category.description: Interactive proofs for shapes, angles, circles, polygons, similarity, and area formulas that can be seen and manipulated.
category.targetAudience: School to Engineering Foundation

visualProofs.title: Volume of a Pyramid: V = (1/3)Bh
visualProofs.shortDescription: Fill a matching prism using three congruent pyramids.
visualProofs.longDescription: A prism with the same base area and height decomposes into three equal-volume pyramids, so one pyramid has one third of the prism volume.

category.title: Mensuration
category.description: Area, volume, surface area, and measurement formula proofs for 2D and 3D shapes.
category.targetAudience: School and competitive-exam learners

visualProofs.title: Shoelace Formula
visualProofs.shortDescription: Draw cross-products as diagonals between coordinate columns and compare signed areas.
visualProofs.longDescription: Writing coordinates in a loop creates two diagonal product sums. Their signed difference equals twice the polygon area.

category.title: Coordinate Geometry
category.description: Interactive visual proofs for distance, midpoint, slope, line equations, circles, transformations, and coordinate-based area formulas.
category.targetAudience: High school, engineering entrance preparation, first-year engineering mathematics

visualProofs.title: Power Integral on [0,1]: integral_0^1 x^n dx = 1/(n+1)
visualProofs.shortDescription: Show areas under successive power curves or use a dimensional partition model.
visualProofs.longDescription: The unit interval power curve can be compared with n+1 dimensional slices, making the reciprocal 1/(n+1) area relationship visible.

category.title: Calculus Visual Proofs
category.description: Interactive visual proofs for limits, derivatives, tangent lines, area under curves, integration, the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, and Taylor series.
category.targetAudience: Senior school, engineering entrance preparation, undergraduate mathematics, engineering mathematics

visualProofs.title: Bayes' Theorem
visualProofs.shortDescription: Use a probability tree and reverse from cause-to-outcome to outcome-to-cause.
visualProofs.longDescription: A two-stage tree shows joint probabilities at the leaves. Conditioning on the observed outcome renormalizes the relevant leaves to reverse the question.
learningOutcomes: Explain normalization by the observed event

visualProofs.title: Binomial Mean: E(X) = np
visualProofs.shortDescription: Show n Bernoulli trials, each contributing expected value p.
visualProofs.longDescription: Each success indicator has expected value p. Adding n independent indicators stacks n equal expectation contributions, giving np.
learningOutcomes: Model a binomial variable as indicators

visualProofs.title: Binomial Variance: np(1-p)
visualProofs.shortDescription: Add independent Bernoulli variances visually.
visualProofs.longDescription: Each independent Bernoulli trial contributes variance p(1-p). Independent contributions add to n p(1-p).

category.title: Probability Proofs

visualProofs.title: Linear Independence
visualProofs.shortDescription: Drag two vectors and show the spanned parallelogram collapsing when they align.
visualProofs.longDescription: Independent vectors span a nonzero-area parallelogram. When one vector becomes a multiple of the other, the area collapses and one direction is lost.
visualProofs.level: High School to Engineering Linear Algebra
learningOutcomes: Connect area collapse to determinant zero

visualProofs.title: Cramer's Rule
visualProofs.shortDescription: Compare determinant-scaled parallelogram areas.
visualProofs.longDescription: Replacing one matrix column by the target vector compares area-scaling factors, so coordinate solutions become determinant ratios.
visualProofs.level: High School to Engineering Linear Algebra
learningOutcomes: Connect column replacement to target vectors

visualProofs.title: Rank as Remaining Independent Directions
visualProofs.shortDescription: Show how many independent directions remain after a transformation.
visualProofs.longDescription: A matrix transformation can preserve a plane, collapse it to a line, or collapse it to a point. Rank counts the independent output directions left.
visualProofs.level: High School to Engineering Linear Algebra

visualProofs.title: Binomial Theorem
visualProofs.shortDescription: Expand an area or cube model, then connect coefficients to Pascal's triangle.
visualProofs.longDescription: Repeated multiplication of a+b creates paths choosing a or b at each factor. Counting equal-choice paths gives the binomial coefficients.

visualProofs.title: Pascal Identity: C(n,r) = C(n-1,r-1) + C(n-1,r)
visualProofs.shortDescription: Split subsets into those containing a selected object and those not containing it.
visualProofs.longDescription: Choosing r objects from n can be counted by first deciding whether a named object is included. The include and exclude cases form the two entries above in Pascal's triangle.
learningOutcomes: Connect subset counts to triangle entries

visualProofs.title: Sum of Cubes: 1^3 + 2^3 + ... + n^3 = [n(n+1)/2]^2
visualProofs.shortDescription: Arrange cubes or layered dot patterns into a square of the triangular number.
visualProofs.longDescription: The first n cubes can be layered into a square whose side length is the nth triangular number, revealing the square on the right side.
learningOutcomes: Connect cube sums to triangular numbers

visualProofs.title: Telescoping Series
visualProofs.shortDescription: Animate cancellation of consecutive positive and negative terms.
visualProofs.longDescription: Adjacent terms cancel in pairs, so the long sum collapses to only the first and last surviving pieces.
learningOutcomes: Explain why only boundary terms remain

visualProofs.title: Standard Deviation Effect
visualProofs.shortDescription: Change spread while keeping the mean fixed and observe the distribution widen.
visualProofs.longDescription: A distribution can keep the same balance point while its data points move farther from the mean. Standard deviation measures that visible widening.

visualProofs.title: Central Limit Theorem
visualProofs.shortDescription: Repeatedly sample and animate the distribution of sample means becoming bell-shaped.
visualProofs.longDescription: Sample means vary less than raw data, and repeated sampling makes their distribution approach a bell shape under broad conditions.
learningOutcomes: Distinguish data distribution from mean distribution

visualProofs.title: Geometric-Series Sum: 1 + r + r^2 + ... = 1/(1-r)
visualProofs.shortDescription: Fill a square or bar using successively shrinking pieces.
visualProofs.longDescription: Each new piece fills the same fraction of what remains. The infinite stack approaches a fixed total of 1/(1-r) when |r| is less than 1.
learningOutcomes: See convergence as filling a region
